summary: Release 1 of a bilingual (English and Amharic), multi-campus Student Information Management System for Ethiopian schools, following SCHOOL_AI_Implementation_Playbook.md. Release 2 features are explicitly excluded.

services.name: SIMS Web and PWA
services.description: Responsive React web application and installable PWA for school staff, guardians, and students; offline support is limited to attendance and marks entry.

services.name: SIMS API
services.description: Node.js API and real-time notification service for tenancy, authentication, academic and operational workflows, integrations, and reporting.

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static type checking to the React application and helps prevent errors as SIMS grows.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses standard JavaScript with the specified React 18 and Vite stack.

questions.rationale: The playbook fixes React 18 and Vite but leaves the frontend language open; TypeScript is recommended for the broad, security-sensitive application.

questions.question: Which frontend framework and tooling should be used?

options.label: React 18 + Vite
options.description: The frontend stack specified by the implementation playbook.

questions.answer: React 18 + Vite, React Router, handwritten responsive CSS (no UI kit or Tailwind), i18n dictionaries for English and Amharic, locally bundled Noto Sans Ethiopic and a Latin font, and vite-plugin-pwa with a custom service worker.
questions.rationale: The implementation playbook explicitly fixes this stack and excludes a UI kit and Tailwind.

questions.question: What should the frontend include?
questions.recommendedChoice: Release 1 SIMS staff workflows and parent/student portals, bilingual UI, responsive layouts, and offline attendance/marks entry
questions.answer: Implement the Release 1 scope in the playbook: organization/campus and academic setup; admissions and enrolment; student, guardian, and document records; timetable; attendance; assessment, grading, ranking, promotion, and report cards; fees and finance; core staff workflows; welfare/conduct; reports; announcements and notifications; parent/student portals; multi-campus administration; and platform administration. Provide English and Amharic UI, responsive phone/tablet/desktop layouts, and PWA offline entry only for attendance and marks. Keep all Release 2 modules out of scope.
questions.rationale: The user asks to build from the supplied Release 1 playbook, which defines the modules and explicitly excludes Release 2.

questions.question: Which language should the backend use?

options.label: JavaScript (ES modules)
options.description: The backend language and module format specified by the playbook.

questions.rationale: The implementation playbook specifies Node.js 20 LTS and JavaScript ES modules.

questions.question: Which backend framework and tooling should be used?

options.label: Node.js 20 + Express
options.description: The API framework and runtime specified by the implementation playbook.

questions.answer: Node.js 20 LTS + Express with mysql2/promise, Knex migrations, Zod, Pino, Helmet, CORS, express-rate-limit, bcrypt, node-cron, JWT access tokens and rotating hashed refresh tokens, and Socket.IO with long-polling fallback.
questions.rationale: The playbook fixes Node.js, Express, the listed supporting packages, and Socket.IO.

questions.question: What should the backend include?
questions.recommendedChoice: Tenant-isolated SIMS API, configurable RBAC, audited workflows, bilingual documents, notifications, and integrations
questions.answer: Implement the API for the Release 1 modules and enforce organization/campus/class scoping from authenticated claims, configurable permissions, guardian verification, append-only audit and financial/marks histories, sensitive-field encryption and audited reveal, Ethiopian calendar and naming requirements, bilingual document generation, and provider interfaces with mock defaults for SMS/email. Use MySQL 8/InnoDB and include no public online admissions, payroll calculations, payment gateway, LMS, bidirectional cloud/local sync, or other Release 2 features.
questions.rationale: This captures the security, integrity, privacy, localization, and scope constraints in the implementation playbook.

questions.question: Which data stores are required?

options.label: MySQL 8
options.description: Primary relational store for SIMS tenant, academic, student, finance, and audit data.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object/file storage for student documents, photos, generated files, and other uploads; use a deployment-appropriate adapter for cloud and school-local installations.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Select only when the project needs no persistence, file/object storage, queues, cache, or associated storage.

questions.rationale: The playbook specifies MySQL 8 and requires document/photo uploads and generated files. File storage must support both cloud and school-local deployment models.

questions.question: Will users sign in to access application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users authenticate to access role- and campus-scoped SIMS features.

options.label: No
options.description: The application has no signed-in user access to its features.

questions.rationale: SIMS requires authenticated staff, guardian, student, and platform administration roles with configurable permissions and tenancy isolation.
